analysis: The only change is a documentation edit to docs/threat-model.yaml in the T-050 mitigation (head lines 1969-1970 per the changed range). It widens the documented accepted inline-video MIME types to data:video/mp4, data:video/x-m4v, data:video/quicktime and data:video/mov. The text adds that the bytes must be an MP4 or QuickTime file. The remaining caps (decoded-byte, duration, frame-pixel, video-count, aggregate) and the rejection of http(s), file and unsupported MIME types are unchanged. The in-memory MemoryBackedVideoAsset mitigation, forbidAll reference restrictions and startup purge are untouched, so the T-050 file-free plaintext property is not weakened by this text. I examined base unit :6, which covers T-047 to T-058 and the T-050 text, and head unit :7, which covers the header and TB-002/TB-003. No other threat entries changed. Remaining integration question: this PR only changes documentation, and the provider media-ingest code (MediaIngest.swift) is not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the code actually enforces the container-signature (magic-byte) check the doc now claims, or that the x-m4v and mov aliases map onto the same in-memory MemoryBackedVideoAsset path with no file or URL fallback. If the code PR is separate, reviewers should confirm that alias MIME types never route through Data.write, FileManager.createFile, or AVAsset(url:), per the T-050 detection_hint. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
